edge_explainer.market_believes: A structurally disadvantaged #3 endpoint-security pure-play: Microsoft bundles Defender effectively free, CrowdStrike out-grows it at 5x the scale, and the CFO chair is empty after a 4th restructuring — worth a laggard multiple (4.5x EV/ARR vs CrowdStrike's ~35x).
edge_explainer.we_believe: The fear is over-charged at the price: the leading indicator (net-new ARR) is genuinely re-accelerating (+55%, 4th straight quarter of acceleration), the Q2 bar was set BELOW the Street (easier to clear), and private-equity takeout precedents (6-9x ARR) imply a soft floor ~20% above spot.
edge_explainer.why_we_might_have_edge: Mostly we DON'T claim one — this is a valuation-asymmetry position, not an information edge. The honest tells cut against management (FCF 'positivity' leaned on a one-time tax add-back; retention quietly de-quantified), which is exactly why it's 4/10 and waits for the print.
edge_explainer.why_it_might_be_priced_in: The structural bear (Microsoft bundling) is real, disclosed, and permanent — the discount may be fully earned. The M&A floor is soft (no live process; the top strategic buyer just bought CyberArk instead).
edge_explainer.what_resolves_it: ~Aug-27 print (fiscal-pattern estimate): the 5th consecutive net-new-ARR growth quarter, the operating-income guide, and whether a permanent CFO is named.
edge_explainer.edge_type: valuation asymmetry + soft M&A floor; NO information/behavioral edge claimed
edge_explainer.mechanism_falsifier: The valuation-asymmetry read dies if the discount persists through TWO clean prints — then the Microsoft-bundling structural bear is being priced correctly and cheap stays cheap.
